## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

# tidy-branches worker

The **assess-only** branch third of the repo tidy-up: a weekly pass over the repo's open branches — run
only when a branch was actually created or pushed in the window — then record the picture. The run's
**Context section is binding scope** — it lists the branches to assess. Work only those; don't enumerate
the repo yourself. GitHub access is **MCP-only** (`mcp__github__*`).

This dimension is read-only: **never delete, push, or merge a branch**, and never open or merge a PR. You
recommend; a human acts. The only thing you write is this task's own tracker issue.

**Never assess the repo's own default branch.** The Context already excludes the known infra branches (the
orphan `conversation-logs` log stream and the `claudinite/maintenance` delivery branch) and the conventional
default names, but a precondition cannot look up the real default branch by name — that exclusion is your
responsibility here.

## 1. Assess each branch

For each branch in the Context list, run the
[single-branch-status](../../skills/single-branch-status/SKILL.md) skill for its verdict — judged by
**content**, never the ref's auto-generated name. Collect:

- one line each for the branches carrying **genuine unmerged work** (`` `branch` — what it carries``);
- the rest collapsed into one `Safe to delete: N — a, b, c` line;
- any **orphaned** branch flagged for a human.

## 2. Reconcile this task's tracker

**Only a run whose picture changed reaches the tracker.** Read the tracker's current body first and compare:
a branch entering or leaving the list, or a verdict that flipped, is news. Verdicts identical to the ones
already in the body are **nothing to record** — leave the body, post no comment, and create no tracker if
none exists. Re-deriving last week's picture is a scan, not a change.

One standing tracker issue per repo, titled exactly `Claudinite tracker: Tidy Branches` — found by that
**exact title, never a fuzzy match**; create it **already closed** when there is something to record and it
is absent — creation always lands an issue open and ignores a `state: closed` argument, so create it and
close it in a second call (never a fresh issue per run, never a bare number that can dangle). Each dimension
keeps its **own** tracker, so three tasks never race to rewrite one body.

Touch it two ways on a run that has something to record:

- **Rewrite the issue body** to today's **dated** snapshot: the branches carrying genuine unmerged work, the
  safe-to-delete count and names, and anything orphaned. The body is the live picture — it replaces last
  week's, it doesn't accumulate.
- **Add a dated comment** with today's status, so the body's snapshots leave a per-run trail.

Keep both short. **Never open, close, or reopen the tracker** — its state carries no meaning. The tracker
only *records* the recommendations; nothing here touches a branch.

`model: sonnet` — superseded / orphaned are judgment calls; the reconcile is mechanical aggregation.

1	// tidy-repo task: tidy-branches — the read-only branch third of the tidy sweep
2	// (per-project-scheduling DESIGN §6). One weekly full sweep over the repo's open
3	// branches: which carry genuine unmerged work, which are safe to delete. Recommends;
4	// never deletes. Worker: task.md. Issues and PRs are separate tasks — one dimension
5	// per task, each with its own trigger, scope, and tracker, so there is no ordering
6	// barrier.
7	//
8	// WEEKLY, and full every time it runs — but it only runs when a branch actually
9	// MOVED in the window. Branch cruft accumulates on a weekly clock, not a daily one,
10	// and the verdict is a standing recommendation for a human rather than a same-day
11	// alert, so the full sweep is a frequency DECLARATION, never a gate trick inside a
12	// daily task (DESIGN §3). What the sweep is NOT is unconditional: re-deriving the
13	// same verdicts over an unchanged pile of branches costs an agent run and produces a
14	// tracker rewrite identical to last week's. Scope stays full because a verdict is
15	// relative to the others (superseded-by, already-in-main); the GATE is newness.
16	//
17	// Self-contained (imports nothing): the whole contract is this default export.
18	
19	// Branches the tidy review must never assess. Beyond the default branch, the orphan
20	// `conversation-logs` branch is a claudinite-growth artifact (the captured-transcript
21	// stream, not project work) — it shares no history with main, so single-branch-status
22	// would flag it "orphaned" for a human on every run. It is infrastructure the tidy
23	// sweep ignores altogether. Kept as a bare literal, not an import: the pack-independence
24	// barrier forbids tidy-repo from reaching into claudinite-growth, and the name is a
25	// fixed, well-known one. The stable maintenance branch is likewise never a tidy target —
26	// it is Claudinite's own standing delivery branch, not project work.
27	const IGNORED_BRANCHES = new Set(['conversation-logs', 'claudinite/maintenance']);
28	
29	// A precondition has no repo handle, so it cannot look up the actual default branch
30	// name to drop it from the candidate set — and the `branches` signal carries every
31	// open branch, the default included. Presuming the conventional default names here
32	// keeps a repo whose only branch is its default from firing this task at all, which is
33	// the whole point of the gate. The worker (task.md) remains the authority that never
34	// assesses the repo's real default branch, so a repo whose default is unconventionally
35	// named is still safe — its default just also becomes a (cheap, read-only) candidate.
36	const PRESUMED_DEFAULT = new Set(['main', 'master']);
37	
38	export default {
39	  id: 'tidy-branches',
40	  frequency: 'weekly',                      // the weekly anchor (DESIGN §2); the full sweep is the declaration
41	  precondition_signals: ['branches'],       // names for the scope, `touched` for the gate
42	  agent_model: 'sonnet',                    // superseded / orphaned / already-in-main are judgment calls on content
43	  expected_outcome: 'none',                 // assess-only: never deletes, pushes, or merges; writes only its tracker
44	  agent_instructions: 'task.md',
45	  agent_execution_timeout: 600,             // one cheap diff-and-merge-base read per branch
46	
47	  // Two gates, in order. Is there a branch worth assessing at all — a repo carrying
48	  // nothing but its default branch (and the infra branches) stays silent. Then: did
49	  // any of them MOVE in the window. An unchanged set of branches yields the same
50	  // verdicts it yielded last run, so re-deriving them buys nothing; the standing
51	  // picture already lives in the tracker. When something did move, scope is still
52	  // the FULL set — a branch's verdict is relative to the others (superseded-by,
53	  // already-in-main), so assessing the new one alone would be assessing it blind.
54	  precondition(signals) {
55	    const assessable = (b) => !IGNORED_BRANCHES.has(b) && !PRESUMED_DEFAULT.has(b);
56	    const branches = (signals.branches?.names ?? []).filter(assessable);
57	    if (!branches.length) return { run: false, reason: 'no branches to assess beyond the default and the infra branches' };
58	
59	    const moved = (signals.branches?.touched ?? []).filter(assessable);
60	    if (!moved.length) {
61	      return { run: false, reason: `no branch created or moved in the window — the standing picture over ${branches.length} branch(es) is unchanged` };
62	    }
63	
64	    return {
65	      run: true,
66	      reason: `${moved.length} branch(es) moved in the window — full sweep over ${branches.length} branch(es)`,
67	      context: [`Branches to assess (read-only — recommend deletions, never delete): ${branches.join(', ')}.`],
68	    };
69	  },
70	};

# Claude Code agent proxy

Outbound HTTPS from this session goes through a local proxy at [REDACTED:env:https_proxy]
(set via HTTPS_PROXY) which tunnels to a policy-enforcing egress proxy. TLS is
re-terminated there, so every tool must trust the CA bundle at
[REDACTED:env:NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS]. The standard CA environment variables, the system trust
store (where possible), a JVM truststore, the Bazel system bazelrc, the
browser NSS store, and gsutil's boto config are already set up.

## Quick diagnosis

1. Run: curl -sS [REDACTED:env:https_proxy]/__agentproxy/status
   It reports proxy state, which trust and git accommodations are active
   (javaTrustStorePath, toolTrustFailureCodes, gitSshRewrite,
   gitConfigConflicts), and the most recent proxy-side failures.
2. Find the failure class below and apply the matching fix; gitConfigConflicts
   codes map to the git section, toolTrustFailureCodes to the JVM section.
3. Never disable TLS verification, never unset HTTPS_PROXY, and do not retry
   organization policy denials (403/407) — report them instead.

## Failure classes and fixes

### "certificate verify failed" / "self-signed certificate in chain" / PKIX errors

The failing tool is not reading the pre-set CA configuration. In order:

- If the tool has a CA flag or env var, point it at [REDACTED:env:NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS]
  (examples: --cacert, SSL_CERT_FILE, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS, REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE,
  AWS_CA_BUNDLE, DENO_CERT, CARGO_HTTP_CAINFO, PIP_CERT, GIT_SSL_CAINFO,
  BUNDLE_SSL_CA_CERT, HEX_CACERTS_PATH, NIX_SSL_CERT_FILE).
- Tool config files override environment variables. If one of these sets its
  own CA or disables verification, point it at the bundle instead:
  pip.conf "cert", npm "cafile" (npm config get cafile), ~/.curlrc "cacert",
  .wgetrc "ca_certificate", conda "ssl_verify", git "http.sslCAInfo",
  gradle.properties / MAVEN_OPTS "-Djavax.net.ssl.trustStore".
- JVM tools (Maven, Gradle, plain Java): when a JDK is present, a truststore
  is built at /root/.ccr/java-truststore.p12 (password "changeit") and
  injected via JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS — confirm javaTrustStorePath is set in the
  status output before pointing a build at it (toolTrustFailureCodes explains
  why it is missing). If the image or the build sets its own trustStore, that
  one wins — import the proxy CA into it with
  keytool -importcert -noprompt -alias ccr-agent-proxy -file /root/.ccr/agent-proxy-ca.crt -keystore <their store>
  or point the build at the ready-made one. Bazel reads the managed block in
  /etc/bazel.bazelrc rather than JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS.

### "405 Method Not Allowed" from the proxy

The tool sent a plain-HTTP (non-CONNECT) request: usually axios older than
1.16.1 (upgrade it) or a tool configured with HTTP_PROXY (unset HTTP_PROXY for
that tool — only HTTPS_PROXY is supported).

### 403 / 407 from the proxy

The destination host is not allowed by your organization's egress policy for
this session. Do not retry or route around it — report the blocked host.
Note: curl hides response bodies on failed CONNECTs; the status endpoint
records the reason.

1	// APPLYING a status transition — the write half of the vocabulary whose read half
2	// is `work-item.mjs`'s decode (tasks-dispatch DESIGN §4, the migration of #1119).
3	//
4	// One rule, and it is why this is not a plain `swapLabel`: the item may wear ANY
5	// engine version's spelling of the status it is leaving. A member's items outlive
6	// its converges, so an item filed as `task:ready` is picked up by an engine that
7	// writes `task:status:waiting-for-executor`, and a swap that named one spelling
8	// would leave the other standing — an item wearing two live statuses, which is the
9	// torn state the janitor exists to repair.
10	//
11	// Writes stay granular (add and remove named labels, never a set-write): with
12	// several executors and a scheduler run moving labels at once, a set-write from a
13	// stale snapshot clobbers a concurrent transition (DESIGN §4).
14	// The removes are UNCONDITIONAL — every spelling of the status being left, not
15	// only the ones the caller's snapshot shows. A caller holds the labels it read
16	// before its own earlier transitions, so filtering on that snapshot would skip
17	// exactly the label this engine just wrote; removing a label an issue does not
18	// carry 404s, which is the end state asked for and therefore success.
19	import { spellingsOf } from './work-item.mjs';
20	
21	// Move `item` out of `fromStatus` (canonical — every spelling of it goes) and into
22	// the label `to`, which is whatever spelling this engine writes.
23	export async function swapStatus(api, gh, repo, item, fromStatus, to) {
24	  await clearStatus(api, gh, repo, item, fromStatus);
25	  return api.addLabel(gh, repo, item.number, to);
26	}
27	
28	// Leave a status without entering another — the close path, where the terminal
29	// label is applied separately.
30	export async function clearStatus(api, gh, repo, item, status) {
31	  for (const label of spellingsOf(status)) {
32	    await api.removeLabel(gh, repo, item.number, label);
33	  }
34	}

1	// The machine-readable records a task's execution leaves in an Actions log
2	// (skill-usage-metrics DESIGN §4.2), and the parsers that read them back.
3	//
4	// TWO FAMILIES, ONE OF THEM HISTORICAL. `claudinite-task-run` was the SLOT
5	// scheduler's own line, one per due task per run; the slot scheduler is retired
6	// (#974) and nothing writes that line any more. The parser stays, and only the
7	// parser: Actions logs from before the retirement are still inside their retention
8	// window, and the usage fold still counts them. Nothing new should be taught this
9	// shape — `claudinite-task-exec` below is the live record.
10	//
11	// The counts these produce are exact within the Actions log retention window, and
12	// that is worth stating next to the capture-derived counts they land beside.
13	
14	// The five things a slot scheduler run could do with a due task. One name per
15	// outcome, used verbatim as the counter key in the aggregate, so there is no
16	// mapping table between "what the run said" and "what the fold counted" to drift.
17	export const TASK_RUN_OUTCOMES = Object.freeze([
18	  // A dispatch issue was filed: an agent session ran this task.
19	  'agent',
20	  // The task ran with NO agent — an `agent_model: none` task (code-work is the
21	  // whole task), or an agentful one whose code-work requested no agent phase.
22	  // Kebab, not the declaration field's `code_work`: this word is a WIRE token,
23	  // constrained to the line format's `[a-z-]+` charset.
24	  'code-work',
25	  // Due, but its precondition said there was nothing to do.
26	  'skipped',
27	  // Its code-work failed; the run converged the task to a needs-human issue.
28	  'failed',
29	  // Due and past its precondition, but no NEW agent run started: this slot was
30	  // already dispatched (exactly-once), an earlier dispatch is still open
31	  // (at-most-one-open), or another task claimed the run exclusively. Work that
32	  // was wanted and did not happen this run.
33	  'deferred',
34	]);
35	
36	// An empty per-task counter row — every outcome present, zeros included, so a row's
37	// shape never depends on which outcomes a task happened to hit.
38	export const emptyTaskRun = () => Object.fromEntries(TASK_RUN_OUTCOMES.map((o) => [o, 0]));
39	
40	// The line format. `v1` is the shape's version: a reader that meets a `v2` line
41	// knows it is looking at something it was not written for, instead of silently
42	// half-parsing it.
43	export const TASK_RUN_TAG = 'claudinite-task-run';
44	const VERSION = 'v1';
45	
46	// Actions stamps every log line with its own timestamp before the command's output,
47	// so the parse tolerates that prefix — without it, a fetched log reads as having
48	// printed nothing at all.
49	const LINE_RE = new RegExp(
50	  String.raw`^(?:\S+\s+)?${TASK_RUN_TAG} ${VERSION} (\S+)/(\S+) \[(\S+)\] ([a-z-]+)\s*$`,
51	);
52	
53	// One line → `{ pack, task, slotId, outcome }`, or null for anything that is not a
54	// record of this version. Deliberately strict: an unknown outcome word is NOT a
55	// record, because counting it would mint a counter key nothing ever reads.
56	// The code phase has been renamed twice, and job logs outlive both renames:
57	// `preprocess` (pre-2026-08-06) and `prework` (pre-2026-08-18) are the earlier
58	// words for what is now `code-work`. Runs logged under either still parse, each
59	// normalized straight to the canonical word.
60	// Exported because the outcome words are also the usage aggregate's counter KEYS,
61	// and that file holds rows written under the older words. Its decode renames them
62	// by this same map, so a rename never silently drops a historical count.
63	export const LEGACY_TASK_RUN_OUTCOMES = Object.freeze({ preprocess: 'code-work', prework: 'code-work' });
64	
65	export function parseTaskRun(line) {
66	  const m = LINE_RE.exec(line);
67	  if (!m) return null;
68	  const [, pack, task, slotId, word] = m;
69	  const outcome = LEGACY_TASK_RUN_OUTCOMES[word] ?? word;
70	  if (!TASK_RUN_OUTCOMES.includes(outcome)) return null;
71	  return { pack, task, slotId, outcome };
72	}
73	
74	// Every record in one job log. The log is the whole job's output — this picks its
75	// own lines out of it and ignores everything else.
76	export function parseTaskRuns(text) {
77	  const out = [];
78	  for (const line of String(text ?? '').split('\n')) {
79	    const rec = parseTaskRun(line);
80	    if (rec) out.push(rec);
81	  }
82	  return out;
83	}
84	
85	// --- executor-side execution records ------------------------------------------
86	// The historical records above say what the retired slot scheduler DID with a due
87	// task; these record what an EXECUTOR SESSION did with the work it ran. Printed by executor-side code
88	// (resolve-dispatch on a terminal verdict, record-exec.mjs at convergence), they
89	// land in the session transcript, ride to the conversation-logs branch with the
90	// executor's capture step, and the usage fold counts them deterministically —
91	// the "task statuses out of the conversation logs" half of the census (owner,
92	// 2026-08-06). Same single-home rule: renderer and parser sit here together.
93	
94	export const TASK_EXEC_STATUSES = Object.freeze([
95	  // The dispatch ran to completion within its ceiling; the issue was closed.
96	  'success',
97	  // The run failed (task failure or ceiling violation); converged to needs-human.
98	  'failed',
99	  // The dispatch named a task the repo no longer carries (file gone, pack
100	  // undeclared) — the executor closed the issue as obsolete. Not a failure.
101	  'task-gone',
102	  // The dispatch was malformed (bad path shape, unparseable declaration) and was
103	  // converged to needs-human without running.
104	  'invalid',
105	]);
106	
107	export const TASK_EXEC_TAG = 'claudinite-task-exec';
108	
109	// The bracketed field is the OCCURRENCE'S IDENTITY, which is a different thing under
110	// each dispatch mechanism: a slot id (`d2026-08-06`) where slots decide what runs, and
111	// the work item's issue number (`#867`) where the queue does. `slotId` keeps its name
112	// for the fielded records that already carry one; what it must never become is a
113	// constant, since it is the only join from a record back to the work it describes.
114	export const renderTaskExec = ({ pack, task, slotId, status }) =>
115	  `${TASK_EXEC_TAG} ${VERSION} ${pack}/${task} [${slotId ?? 'unknown'}] ${status}`;
116	
117	const EXEC_LINE_RE = new RegExp(
118	  String.raw`(?:^|\s)${TASK_EXEC_TAG} ${VERSION} (\S+)/(\S+) \[(\S+)\] ([a-z-]+)\s*$`,
119	);
120	
121	export function parseTaskExec(line) {
122	  const m = EXEC_LINE_RE.exec(line);
123	  if (!m) return null;
124	  const [, pack, task, slotId, status] = m;
125	  if (!TASK_EXEC_STATUSES.includes(status)) return null;
126	  return { pack, task, slotId, status };
127	}
128	
129	export function parseTaskExecs(text) {
130	  const out = [];
131	  for (const line of String(text ?? '').split('\n')) {
132	    const rec = parseTaskExec(line);
133	    if (rec) out.push(rec);
134	  }
135	  return out;
136	}
